relevance.rationale: This is the paper that writes the 4_1 state integral as an explicit BILINEAR combination of a q-series and a q-tilde-series, and identifies the resulting power series as Kontsevich-Soibelman admissible with the Nahm/gluing equation as its q -> 1 limit. Both are objects the folio already reasons about without this anchor: conj:modular-s-transform-q-q-tilde (D14) conjectures that every Hecke quantity continues to the modular parameter and pairs q with q-tilde, citing only kashaev1997 / neumann-zagier1985 / kashaev-tirkkonen2014; and conj:stokes-dt-bps-bridge + thm:aomega-fourone-dt-count run the 4_1 resurgent-Stokes/DT route on the Garoufalidis-Gu-Marino q-series whose origin is exactly the factorisation proved here. The sibling garoufalidis-kashaev2015 ('Evaluation of state integrals at rational points') is already registered; this earlier companion, which supplies the factorisation itself, is not. Corpus-grep: no ref() entry, no title match, no Lean -- Ref:.

keyResults.statement: The Andersen-Kashaev state integral of the figure-eight knot factorises as I_{4_1}(b) = -(i/2)(q/q~)^{1/24}( b·G(q)g(q~) - b^{-1}·G(q~)g(q) ), an explicit bilinear pairing of two q-hypergeometric series evaluated at q and at the modular partner q~.
keyResults.useForFolio: A proved, explicit instance of the q <-> q~ pairing that conj:modular-s-transform-q-q-tilde asserts abstractly (its Open R&D item 1 asks precisely for framework quantities with well-defined modular continuation). It is also the source of the two 4_1 q-series whose Stokes matrix supplies the certified S^+(0)_{01} = 3 datum feeding A_omega(4_1).

keyResults.statement: F_{A,B}(q^{-1}, x) = F~_{A,B}(q, x) — inverting q exchanges the series with its modular partner.
keyResults.useForFolio: Directly relevant to the folio's bar-vs-S-transform bookkeeping: the D14 block argues that only q_0^{-1} ~ 0.901 lands in the upper half-plane, so the modular sector is intrinsically bar-symmetric. This lemma is the literature statement of that bar/modular exchange at the level of the q-series themselves.

keyResults.statement: F is an admissible power series in the sense of Kontsevich-Soibelman [KS11, §6]; the limit omega(x) = lim_{q->1} omega(q,x) exists and satisfies the Nahm/gluing equation (1 - omega)^B = (-1)^A x·omega^A.
keyResults.useForFolio: Bridges the 4_1 q-series to the Kontsevich-Soibelman wall-crossing framework that conj:stokes-dt-bps-bridge invokes when it identifies the Stokes constant with Omega_DT — a named, published link between the knot's q-series and the DT machinery, rather than an asserted one.

proposedActions.rationale: Orphan; three distinct downstream uses. The companion garoufalidis-kashaev2015 is already registered, so the key should follow that naming.

conj:modular-s-transform-q-q-tilde asserts modular continuation and a q<->q~ duality with no explicit factorisation anchor in its cites[] (kashaev1997, neumann-zagier1985, kashaev-tirkkonen2014). Cor. 1.7 is a proved instance.
conj:stokes-dt-bps-bridge invokes Kontsevich-Soibelman DT data for the knot's q-difference structure; Cor. 1.6(b) is the published statement that these knot q-series are KS-admissible.

relevance.rationale: Garoufalidis-Kashaev, 'From state integrals to q-series': a detailed proof, for a family of one-dimensional state integrals I_{A,B}(b) = int Phi_b(x)^B exp(-A pi i x^2) dx, that such integrals equal finite sums of products of a q-series and a q-tilde-series, with q = exp(2 pi i b^2) and q-tilde = exp(-2 pi i / b^2); the mechanism is the factorized structure of Faddeev's quantum dilogarithm Phi_b = (e^{2 pi b(x+c_b)}; q)_infty / (e^{2 pi b^{-1}(x-c_b)}; q-tilde)_infty together with its pole structure and the residue theorem, and the worked applications are the state-integral invariants of the 4_1 and 5_2 knots. That factorization IS the object the corpus's live c_3 bar-odd front is built on: docs/audits/2026-07-25-5two-gk-bridge-attack.md (beans qou-reat, o3cv, jtii, exes) works entirely with 'the GK bilinear block pairing Z = sum M_{sigma sigma'} B_sigma(q) B-tilde_{sigma'}(q-tilde)' and its state-integral dressing, and the corpus's registered sources for it are GK 1411.6062 (evaluation at rational points) and GGM (peacock patterns) -- the theorem that produces the bilinear q / q-tilde block form in the first place has no ref() entry, and both of its worked knots are exactly the corpus's two.

keyResults.statement: The one-dimensional state integral I_{A,B}(b) equals a finite sum of products of a q-series and a q-tilde-series, obtained by residues from the factorized form of Phi_b, with generating series F_{A,B}(q,x).
keyResults.useForFolio: The theorem that licenses the bilinear block form Z = sum M B_sigma(q) B-tilde_{sigma'}(q-tilde) on which the 5_2 GK-bridge attack's 440 pre-registered entry comparisons and its block-row-selection successor are built; currently used with no citation for the factorization itself.

keyResults.statement: Explicit q / q-tilde factorizations of the state-integral invariants of the 4_1 and 5_2 knots.
keyResults.useForFolio: The 4_1 and 5_2 block series the corpus's bilinear-bridge probes construct and compare against the Habiro-face targets; the corpus's gate for the 4_1 case currently cites the b=1 closed form of GK 1411.6062 instead.

proposedActions.rationale: The factorization theorem underlying the corpus's entire GK bilinear-block programme (4_1 and 5_2 both worked) has no bibliography entry, while the downstream GK and GGM papers do.
The block asserting the Stokes/DT state-integral bridge should cite the theorem that produces the q / q-tilde bilinear block structure it uses.

Record the scope honestly: Thm 1.1 is proved for the ONE-dimensional family I_{A,B}; the general multi-dimensional statement is described as well known to experts but not proved here. Any corpus use beyond 4_1 / 5_2 should say which case it is relying on.
